name: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

date.note: Preprint submission date; the PRL publication (108, 171803) followed in 2012.

title: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

claim.quote: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

summary.plain: Daya Bay measured a non-zero value of the neutrino mixing angle θ13, with a significance of 5.2σ. It compared antineutrinos from six nuclear reactors in detectors at near and far sites: fewer arrived at the far site, about 1.6 kilometres away, than expected without oscillation.
summary.technical: Six antineutrino detectors in two near (flux-weighted baselines 470 m and 576 m) and one far (1648 m) underground halls; 43,000 ton-GW_th-day livetime exposure in 55 days, 10416 (80376) electron antineutrino candidates at the far (near) hall. The ratio of observed to expected antineutrinos at the far hall is R = 0.940 ± 0.011(stat) ± 0.004(syst); a rate-only analysis finds sin²2θ13 = 0.092 ± 0.016(stat) ± 0.005(syst) in a three-neutrino framework, and a non-zero θ13 with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations.

why_it_matters.value: The paper's introduction says that of the three mixing angles θ13 was the least known before this result; Daya Bay reports a non-zero value with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations.
why_it_matters.quote: The Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment has measured a non-zero value for the neutrino mixing angle θ13 with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations. ... Of these mixing angles, θ13 is the least known.

key_value_text.value: far-hall observed/expected ratio R = 0.940 ± 0.011(stat) ± 0.004(syst); non-zero θ13 with a significance of 5.2σ
